To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
uveal and cutanean melanoma cells differ in their interaction with the vitronectin matrix.

1) uveal melanoma and cutaneous melanomas have a different adhesion level and speed of migration on vitronectins, 2) αvβ5 and β1, 6‐branches are important for adhesion of all cells to the vitronectin and 3) the αvβ3 is involved in the adhesion and migration of cutaneous melanoma only

(i) primary uveal and primary cutaneous melanoma differ in their ability to adhere to vitronectins and to migrate through vitronectin coated surfaces; (ii) the β1,6 branching in N‐glycane is important in the adhesion process, but not in migration; (iii) integrin αv is important in both uveal and cutaneal melanoma, but the β3 and β5 subunits play different roles.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the integrins and N‐oligosacharides that are involved in melanoma cell interaction and migration on vitronectins, which is important for their further use in the development of anti‐melanoma therapy.
the differences between primary uveal melanoma and cutaneous melanomas and their interaction with vitrionectin.
the identification of a novel adhesion mechanism in primary uveal melanoma, which is based on the expression of αvβ1 integrin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adhesion of uveal melanomas to vitronectins is not as efficient as cutaneous melanomas and is mediated by a variety of integrins.
cutaneous melanoma and uveal melanoma have different mechanisms of interaction with vitronctein.
the uveal and cutaneum melanoma cell lines differ significantly in their interaction with integrin αv and vitronectin in terms of adhesion, but they are similar in their migration efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
uveal and cutaneus melanoma cells interact with vitronecton differently.
the interaction of uveal and cutaneal melanomas with vitronectins is different, but the mechanisms of this difference remain to be elucidated.

the adhesion and migration of uveal melanomas are less dependent on vitronectins, and this is not due to the lack of expression of αvβ3 or αvβ5 but rather due to the reduced expression of αv integrins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction of uveal and cutaneal melanoma cells with vitronectins is different, but the role of αvβ3 and αvβ5 in this process is less pronounced in uveal melanomas.
the interaction of primary melanoma cells with vitronectins is a very complex process and it cannot be explained by a single mechanism.
vitronectin may be a useful substrate for the study of melanoma cell migration in vitro.
